errors.english: either one or both of the things to be understood [note: the probandum] and the thing that makes them understood [note: the reason]
errors.why: go bar bya ba / go bar byed pa here are the two parties, the one to be informed (respondent) and the one who informs (proponent), as the following list of 'unestablished for the proponent / for both' shows; not probandum and reason.

fix.find: either one or both of the things to be understood [note: the probandum] and the thing that makes them understood [note: the reason]
fix.replace: either one or both of the one to be informed [note: the respondent] and the one who informs [note: the proponent]

errors.english: the arising occurs through the equality of the supporting cause and the object
errors.why: yul mtshungs pa means 'having the same location' as the supporting cause; the effect arises in the same place as its substrate, not through an equality of cause and object.

errors.english: This also applies when (both are unestablished or doubted).
errors.why: The side only opens this lemma; the English supplies a conclusion (that it too is inconclusive) which the next side contradicts by assigning the case to the contradictory reason.

note: A competent rendering of a difficult Pramāṇa commentary, but the note misidentifies the two parties in the asiddha classification and a few phrases are loosened.

errors.english: the ritual characteristics of the bali and the mandala offerings
errors.why: 'khor lo mchod pa is the cakra worship (the circle/feast offering of the yoginīs), not a mandala offering.

fix.find: the bali and the mandala offerings
fix.replace: the bali and the circle (cakra) worship

errors.english: Through (bali) sacrificial food offerings
errors.why: lha bshos is the food offering to the deity (naivedya), distinct from the gtor ma (bali) treated in the same chapter.

note: The verse list of offerings and the chapter transition are rendered faithfully; the colophon mislabels the cakra worship.

errors.english: By doing so, the deity displaced his own heart with a mind of pride.
errors.why: The Blessed One, with the three verses, dispels the contempt that arose in the deity's mind and the deity's own pride; the deity is not the agent.

fix.find: By doing so, the deity displaced his own heart with a mind of pride.
fix.replace: With these verses the Blessed One dispelled that contempt and the deity's own proud mind.

note: The verses on aśubha and the signless are well rendered; the framing sentence about the deity's pride has the agent wrong.

errors.english: residing in the realm of majesty
errors.why: gzi brjid kyi dbyings su mnyam par zhugs pa is absorption in the fire-element (tejodhātu) meditation, the standard detail of the Tiṣya/Puṣya story.

fix.find: residing in the realm of majesty
fix.replace: absorbed in the meditative attainment of the fire element (tejodhātu)

errors.english: He pleased seven hundred and twenty-seven [note: buddhas].
errors.why: With the previous side ('stong phrag bdun cu') the number is seventy-seven thousand buddhas; 'seven hundred and twenty' is invented.

note: The eon and buddha counts of the Sthavira reckoning are all correct; the samādhi term and the opening number are wrong.

errors.english: The source for this is stated in the (Dronpa) The Traveler: "Without going outside, they shall be separated in this manner like two travelers."
errors.why: 'dron pa is 'the guest', not a text title: the source says the guest is not to be put outside, but the space is to be divided in two with the guest.

fix.find: The source for this is stated in the (Dronpa) The Traveler: "Without going outside, they shall be separated in this manner like two travelers."
fix.replace: The source for this is the statement: "The guest is not to be sent outside; rather, divide the space in two with the guest in this way."

errors.english: bird-shelters
errors.why: bya skyibs is a lean-to or covered porch/shed, not a shelter for birds.

note: The sahaśayyā rule and the Upāli citations are correctly handled; one source citation is turned into an invented text title.

errors.english: This text explains the characteristics of flawed scripture and the principles of logical reasoning. It defines the characteristic of a flawed scripture as one that is inherently impure in its nature.
errors.why: The side opens only with the last item of a list, 'the characteristic of teaching utterly impure scripture'; the summary sentences are the translator's own.

fix.find: This text explains the characteristics of flawed scripture and the principles of logical reasoning. It defines the characteristic of a flawed scripture as one that is inherently impure in its nature.
fix.replace: ...and the characteristic of teaching utterly impure scripture.

errors.english: This covers anything that can be perceived or thought about.
errors.why: No such sentence in the Tibetan.

errors.english: regarding the characteristic of universal observation and its examples
errors.why: The Tibetan is 'observation of similarity to another' (gzhan dang mthun par dmigs pa), a different item from 'complete similarity', which the English conflates with it.

errors.english: By abandoning the afflictions of both the mundane and supramundane worlds
errors.why: Mundane and supramundane qualify the abandonment (by mundane and supramundane paths), not afflictions belonging to a supramundane world.

note: The core argument on similarity/dissimilarity of examples is roughly right, but the translation adds framing sentences and blurs the technical list of characteristics.

errors.english: the fourth-class (dha) becomes the first-class (da) as if the change had not occurred
errors.why: The rule makes the initial third-class d become its fourth (dh) (duh > dhuk), the opposite direction.

fix.find: the fourth-class (dha) becomes the first-class (da) as if the change had not occurred
fix.replace: the initial third-class (da) becomes its fourth-class (dha), as if the following change had not occurred

errors.english: the vowel (u) is substituted by the word (va)
errors.why: In anaḍuh the syllable va is replaced by u (samprasāraṇa), not u by va.

fix.find: the vowel (u) is substituted by the word (va)
fix.replace: the syllable (va) is replaced by the vowel (u)

errors.english: (godhukkamyati) he desires a milk-cow
errors.why: godhuh means a cow-milker (herdsman), not a milch cow.

errors.english: (vakamyati) he desires a bird
errors.why: In this series of r-stems with visarga the word is vār, 'water'; 'bird' (vi) does not fit the rule being illustrated.

errors.english: and for the roots ending in (drish) and others
errors.why: The rule covers the ca-group as well as dṛś etc. (which is why vāc becomes vāk); the ca-group is dropped.

note: The examples are mostly identified correctly, but several sandhi rules are stated backwards or garbled, which matters in a grammar.

errors.english: a learner (Sekha)
errors.why: In a Sanskrit Abhidharma commentary the term is śaikṣa; Sekha is the Pali form.

note: A faithful rendering of the discussion of the six types of arhat and the samayavimukta's causes of falling away.

errors.english: Like an only child and a protector of elephants,
errors.why: bu gcig ma is the mother of an only child (the simile of undistracted watchfulness), not the child.

fix.find: Like an only child and a protector of elephants,
fix.replace: Like the mother of an only child and an elephant-keeper,

errors.english: The places of coming, going, and staying are the cessation of the place of birth.
errors.why: The line correlates going, coming and staying with arising, abiding and ceasing; it does not speak of a cessation of the birthplace.

errors.english: If that body is held captive within the house
errors.why: It is the wind (de) that is imprisoned in the house of the body, and the mind that kills the 'person'; the English makes the body the captive and the mind's person the victim.

errors.english: Does not liberate because the self is not bound here.
errors.why: The line says that since there is no bondage here there is no liberation either; it is not a statement that conceptualizing fails to liberate.

note: The doctrinal vocabulary of the verses is mostly right, but several similes and line constructions are misconstrued.

errors.english: the glorious (Takkiraja) King of the Lustful
errors.why: gnod mdzes kyi rgyal po is Sumbharāja, the krodha of the nadir; Ṭakkirāja ('dod pa'i rgyal po) was already placed earlier.

fix.find: the glorious (Takkiraja) King of the Lustful

errors.english: (Ishtaraja) King of Desires
errors.why: 'dod pa'i rgyal po among the ten krodhas is Ṭakkirāja; 'Ishtaraja' is not the name.

errors.english: the Buddha-Eye will become like that of the Great Vajra Holder
errors.why: sangs rgyas spyan is most likely the goddess Buddhalocanā, who becomes like Mahāvajradhara, not a 'Buddha-Eye like that of' Vajradhara.

note: The visualization sequence and directional placements are clear and mostly right; some deity names in the krodha circle are wrong.
